question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -4 \\ 4 & 14 & -16 \\ 3 & 13 & -11\end{aligned}]
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ given above, what is the value of ${l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{23}?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's apply our standard LU factorization algorithm.

We reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form to obtain the matrix $U,$ as usual. However, instead of writing zeros below the main diagonal, we will instead write down the entries of the matrix $L.$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -4 \\ 4 & 14 & -16 \\ 3 & 13 & -11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -4 \\ \,\,4\,\, & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 13 & -11\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -4 \\ \,\,4\,\, & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -4 \\ \,\,4\,\, & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & \,2\, & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,U=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, since ${l}_{32}=2$ and ${u}_{23}=0,$ we get

$$
{l}_{32}\cdot {u}_{23}=2\cdot 0=0.
$$
